findings.location: Paragraph 2 (translation) — sentence: "Il y avait peu d’épiceries générales et, autant que possible, ils vivaient aussi autonome que possible."
findings.source_quote: There were few general stores and as much as possible they lived as self-sufficiently as they could.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct grammar/number agreement and improve idiomatic phrasing while preserving meaning. For example: "Il y avait peu d'épiceries générales et, autant que possible, ils vivaient aussi de façon autonome." or "...ils vivaient aussi autonomement que possible."
findings.translation_quote: Il y avait peu d’épiceries générales et, autant que possible, ils vivaient aussi autonome que possible.

findings.location: Paragraph beginning with "Je crains que beaucoup aujourd’hui..." — sentence: "...au pire cela empêche l’observation de nombreux passages bibliques qui commandent le « les-uns-les-autres »."
findings.source_quote: At the very least it can create a sense of isolation, and at the worst it hinders many of the “one-anothering” Bible passages from being followed.
findings.suggested_fix: The phrase "les-uns-les-autres" is awkward in French. Render the concept more naturally while preserving the English author's intent (the New Testament 'one another' commands). Suggested rephrasing: "...au pire cela empêche l'observation de nombreux passages bibliques qui commandent de 'se porter les uns les autres'" or "...qui ordonnent les relations mutuelles ('les uns envers les autres')."
findings.translation_quote: au pire cela empêche l’observation de nombreux passages bibliques qui commandent le « les-uns-les-autres ».

findings.location: Paragraph: "Le contraire de l’isolement" — sentence: "Ce mot est la communion."
findings.source_quote: There is another word which has a Christian connotation that is even better. That word is fellowship.
findings.suggested_fix: "Fellowship" is translated as "la communion", which in French can strongly connote the Eucharist. To preserve the author's theological intent (koinonia as Christian mutual fellowship), consider a wording that avoids sacramental ambiguity, for example: "Ce mot est la communion fraternelle" or "Ce mot est la koinonia (la communion fraternelle)."
